newsitem.title: USA: Senate digital TV conversion bill introduced.
newsitem.headline: Senate digital TV conversion bill introduced.

text.p: Senate Commerce Committee Chairman John McCain Tuesday introduced a bill to set deadlines for the conversion of the U.S. television system to digital broadcasting.

McCain, an Arizona Republican, said the bill was needed because rules recently adopted by the Federal Communications Commission on digital conversion are not binding on more than 90 percent of all television stations.

He said the FCC also has not adopted any way to verify compliance with the schedule and there is no rule requiring that television licensees return their current analogue channels on any given date so they can be auctioned.

"We cannot be lax in our duty to guarantee that consumers enjoy both the telecommunications benefits of digital television and the economic benefits of the analogue channels' auction revenues," McCain said.

McCain's bill would require licensees of the four largest commercial broadcast networks, including affiliates, serving the 10 largest broadcast markets to provide digital video programming no later than May 1, 1999.
Licensees of commercial television stations providing digital video programming would have to relinquish any analogue spectrum assigned to them by the FCC by January 1, 2006.
